title: `custom_template` option in `export_presets.cfg` should prefer project-relative paths since it's in version control
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in v4.3.stable.flathub [77dcf97d8]

### System information

Godot v4.3.stable (77dcf97d8) - Freedesktop SDK 24.08 (Flatpak runtime) - X11 - GLES3 (Compatibility) - Mesa Intel(R) HD Graphics 5500 (BDW GT2) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-5300U CPU @ 2.30GHz (4 Threads)

### Issue description

Users may want to compile their own custom templates. Often one would want to build a custom template specific for the project, for optimization purposes (e.g. to minify web builds). So, naturally, I would place the file within the project, and set it to `custom_template` in `export_presets.cfg`.

The issue is that `export_presets.cfg` is meant to be in version control. Which means it should never contain any absolute paths when it points to any file within the project! This ruins the intended convenience of the feature, making it pointless.

Other fields like `export_path` are already allowing project-relative values. But `custom_template` sets it as an absolute value even for files inside the project, and won't accept relative values. Even if you manually input it as a relative path, it just won't work, and it will use the default template with not even a warning.

Proposed solution:
- ~~Allow the field as both absolute or relative path, preferring relative.~~
- If using the file select UI button, make it so project files are input as relative paths, and absolute if outside the project.
- ~~If that field is not empty, raise an error or at least a warning if the custom template is not used for any reason (e.g. not found).~~

### Steps to reproduce

1. Build or use some custom export template. Make sure you can identify the output, e.g. by having a different `.wasm` size from the default.
2. Set it to e.g. the `custom_template/release` in `export_presets.cfg`. If you use the UI, note it's added as absolute path.
3. Change it to a relative path, either manually or by editing the field, as you don't want absolute paths in version control.
4. Export the project using the custom template (mark debug or release accordingly). Note how the size indicates the default template was used instead, with no error or warning.

EDIT: ~~Just tested again, and it worked as expected. Sorry, I have no idea what happened.~~
I'll still leave this open for the suggestion to prefer relative paths in the file picker if it's within the project, but feel free to close if you disagree.
EDIT 2: See comment below.
